title: Aligning text
summary: start, center, end and justify on the same text, and why text-align does not move boxes.
explanation: text-align lines up the text inside a box: start (left in English), center, end, or justify, which stretches the spaces so both edges are straight. Use start for paragraphs; center works for short headings and buttons, not for long text.

It aligns inline content only. It will not centre a box that has a width: that needs margin-inline: auto, flex or grid. People often put text-align: center on a card and wonder why the card stays left.
justify in a narrow column leaves big gaps between words, called rivers. Look at the fourth box.
tryThis: Change .end's text-align to right, then add dir: rtl to it in Items: end follows the writing direction, right does not.
Add text-align: center to .grid: every box inherits it except those that set their own.
Narrow the grid's max-width to 400px and watch the justified box's gaps widen.

children.text: start: the ragged edge is on the right, which is easiest to read.
center: fine for a short heading or a call to action.
end: used for numbers, dates and captions on the far side.
justify: both edges are straight, but a narrow column gets wide gaps between words.
